title: Why You'd Never Want To Meet An Orca

scenes.notes: Wild killer whales could kill you easily. They never have.
Not because they can't. A big male is eight metres long, as heavy as four cars, and its fin alone is as tall as you.

scenes.notes: It hits fifty-six kilometres an hour. An Olympic swimmer manages eight. You, maybe three. From fifty metres out, it reaches you in three seconds.
And you'd never meet just one. Every pod has its own calls, its own menu, its own plan.

scenes.notes: In Antarctica, a pod charges an ice floe together, and the wave washes the seal straight off. You'd go too.

scenes.notes: Off South Africa, the shark you're scared of started washing up missing one organ. The liver. Orcas flipped them and took it.
The surviving great whites fled for months. If they run, what chance do you have?
In twenty nineteen, off Western Australia, a pod brought down the biggest animal on Earth. An adult blue whale, a thousand times your weight.
So why has something this fast and this smart never come for you?
Maybe you taste bad? Nobody's ever proven that. Too small to bother with? You're about the size of the seals they eat.
The best answer is culture. Orcas eat what their mothers taught them. And no orca mother has ever taught her calf to eat you.
Comforting, right? Except since twenty twenty, orcas off Spain and Portugal have been ramming sailboats and snapping off their rudders.
About seven boats have sunk. Nobody knows why.
Maybe they just haven't decided about you yet. And that matters, because...
